read.thesis: Asset-light hotel franchisor guides 2026 net rooms growth to 4.5%-5% on a record 610,000-room pipeline, with 2026 adjusted EBITDA of $5.8-5.9B, though supply signals are mostly unchanged and RevPAR growth is only 1.5%-2.5%.

capex.quote: We expect $1 billion to $1.1 billion of investment spending in '26, similar to 2025 spending, excluding Citizen Now.

triggers.label: Pipeline record 610,000 rooms
triggers.quote: our pipeline had grown to a record 610,000 rooms, up 2% from the prior quarter and up 6% from the prior year

triggers.label: Net rooms growth 4.5%-5% in 2026
triggers.quote: For full year 2026, net rooms growth is expected to accelerate up to 4.5% to 5%.

triggers.label: Co-brand card fees up ~35%
triggers.quote: our guidance does include a meaningful expected year-over-year increase of around 35% in co-branded credit card fees
triggers.highlight: around 35% in co-branded credit card fees

triggers.label: Royalty rate raised on card deal
triggers.quote: we have increased Marriott International, Inc.'s royalty rate
triggers.highlight: increased Marriott International, Inc.'s royalty rate

triggers.label: Government RevPAR down ~30% in Q4
triggers.quote: Government RevPAR was down over 30% during the forty-three-day U.S. Government shutdown

guidance.quote: For full year 2026, net rooms growth is expected to accelerate up to 4.5% to 5%.
For full year 2026, we expect similar global RevPAR growth to 2025 between 1.5% to 2.5%.
For the full year, fee revenues could rise 8% to 10% to $5.9 billion to $5.96 billion.
Full year adjusted EBITDA could increase between 8% to 10%, to roughly $5.8 billion to $5.9 billion.
leads to expected full year adjusted diluted EPS growth between 13% to 15%.
We expect $1 billion to $1.1 billion of investment spending in '26, similar to 2025 spending, excluding Citizen Now.
In 2026, we expect another year of strong capital returns of over $4.3 billion.
For the first quarter, Global RevPAR could increase 1% to 2%
